q: What is the true operational definition of I_STD in eq. 3 of Lengert et al. 2018, and does the compiled AutoFoci.jar match the paper text? (Our per-cell pixel-SD reading gives w in [0.30, 1.05], but the paper reports w in [0.9, 1.2] --- a ~3x disagreement in an exponent factor that gates every downstream foci count.)
basis: This replication reproduced the headline rho=0.90 only by discarding eq. 3 and using w=1 (plain geometric mean). Direct implementation of eq. 3 yielded rho=0.555, off by 0.35 from the paper. Either eq. 3 is under-specified in the paper text or the compiled jar implements a different formula. This gap was not chased at replication time and is the single largest unresolved technical question left by this run.
next_steps: (a) Read repo/AutoFoci/src to reverse-engineer the exact I_STD definition used by the jar (source-of-truth); (b) run AutoFoci.jar on the same 473-object rated set and diff its per-object combined OEP against our Python reimplementation to find where they diverge; (c) email Lengert / Loebrich (or file a GitHub issue on nleng/AutoFoci) with the diff to request definitional confirmation; (d) if the jar and text disagree, publish an errata-worthy technical note.

q: Does OEP generalise across imaging platforms, or was it silently tuned to Lengert-lab microscope PSF, pixel size, and antibody batch? OEP hard-codes six numerical constants (top-hat disk 10 px, inertia disk 3 px, LoG kernel weights, min area 3 px, intensity factor 1.1, local-max radius 3 px) whose values presumably reflect a single lab's imaging stack. Downstream low-dose kinetic conclusions from other labs using AutoFoci may inherit optimistic bias.
basis: All 344 rated test images and 473 rated objects come from one lab, one microscope, one antibody batch. This replication did not probe robustness across pixel sizes or PSF widths. The paper itself does not do a cross-platform sensitivity analysis. Yet AutoFoci is being adopted (per Google Scholar) by other DSB-repair groups whose imaging stacks differ.
next_steps: (a) Apply the Python reimpl. to independent public DSB foci datasets (IRIF-net, Human Protein Atlas microscopy subsets containing gammaH2AX images) and measure rho degradation; (b) sensitivity-sweep each of the six constants +/-50% on the Lengert data and quantify rho impact; (c) re-optimise constants on an independent lab's rated data and compare against the Lengert defaults; (d) if constants must be re-fit per lab, propose an OEP-fit-per-experiment protocol and add it to the AutoFoci docs.

q: Can a small learned classifier (logistic regression on the 22 features, random forest, or a shallow CNN on 32x32 nuclear crops) match or exceed OEP's rho=0.89 on the 473-object set, and --- critically --- does any such classifier also produce the clean *bimodal* score distribution that gives AutoFoci its practical utility (per-experiment human-tunable threshold)? The paper's contribution is not merely a rho number; it is the interpretable bimodal structure. A learned model that beats rho but loses bimodality would not replace OEP in practice.
basis: OEP is a hand-crafted 2010-era feature product. Modern classifiers with 473 labeled examples could plausibly match its ranking accuracy under cross-validation. But the biological workflow depends on the valley-threshold heuristic, which requires a bimodal score. No published work has done this head-to-head with bimodality as a first-class evaluation criterion.
next_steps: (a) 5-fold CV of logistic regression, random forest (100 trees), and a small ResNet-18 on 32x32 object crops, using features.csv as input; (b) report Spearman rho AND Hartigan's dip test for unimodality on each classifier's score histogram; (c) write up as a benchmark case study for 'interpretable structure vs. predictive power' in bioimage analysis; (d) release the 5-fold splits + baseline scripts as a mini-benchmark others can extend.

q: What is the true false-negative rate of the AutoFoci valley threshold across the low-dose (12--50 mGy) tail of the DSB dose-response, and how much does that FNR bias the fitted repair-kinetics parameters in Fig. 4 of the paper? The valley threshold gave us 100% precision but only 56% recall on the 473-object set. The paper's low-dose conclusions rest on counting foci at doses where expected foci-per-cell is <1, so a 44% FNR floor could non-trivially bend the fitted rate constants.
basis: This replication established that the valley threshold is conservative (precision=1.00, recall=0.562, F1=0.720). The paper never reports an FNR-vs-dose curve or an FNR-corrected repair-rate fit. C6 (biological kinetics) was not tested here because the raw kinetic image set is not public. This is arguably the most consequential un-probed claim in the paper.
next_steps: (a) Simulate synthetic foci at known intensities spanning the low-dose spectrum (Poisson-distributed count, log-normal intensity), run the reimpl. through OEP + valley thresholding, and quantify FNR-vs-signal-strength; (b) re-fit the paper's Fig. 4 exponential repair-kinetics model on synthetic data with a 0--50% FNR prior and measure how much the low-dose rate constant moves; (c) if FNR is signal-dependent, propose a Horvitz--Thompson-style FNR-corrected count estimator; (d) request the Fig. 4 raw images from the authors (or from LUCID collaborators) and re-fit end-to-end.

q: Is the compactness factor in eq. 1 actually contributing signal to OEP, or is OEP dominated entirely by top-hat x LoG? The paper introduces compactness as a shape term meant to discriminate true foci from linear/diffuse background, but never ablates it. If compactness is inert, the OEP parameter surface (and therefore its per-lab tuning burden, per Q2) shrinks meaningfully.
basis: Log(OEP) = log(top-hat) + log(LoG) + log(compactness) - log(nucleus mean). This decomposition is linear in log-space and directly amenable to variance decomposition. This replication implemented all four factors faithfully but did not do the ablation, so the marginal contribution of compactness is unknown even though the data (features.csv) is on disk.
next_steps: (a) Compute rho for OEP with compactness removed (top-hat x LoG / nucleus-mean only), top-hat alone, LoG alone, compactness alone --- 4 easy re-scoring runs on the existing features.csv; (b) run an ANOVA-style variance decomposition on log(OEP); (c) if compactness contributes <0.02 to rho, propose an OEP-lite two-factor variant and re-check that its log-score distribution is still bimodal (the property that makes AutoFoci practically useful, per Q3); (d) if bimodality survives OEP-lite, the pipeline gets simpler, faster, and easier to port across labs.
